$comment: Project-scoped MCP servers for WeVolunteer. Committed deliberately, so the
restricted configuration is the default a developer gets rather than
something each person has to remember to apply.
NO CREDENTIALS HERE. Better Stack authenticates by browser OAuth on first
use; Claude Code stores the resulting token outside the repository. A Better
Stack API token must never be added to this file.
X-MCP-Tools-Only is an ALLOWLIST, and under an ADMIN credential it is THE
BOUNDARY rather than defence in depth — there is no server-side restriction
left underneath it. Three things about it used to be unknown. All three were
settled on 2026-08-29 by bin/betterstack-mcp-audit.mjs, which only ever sends
initialize and tools/list and never calls a tool:
1. [VERIFIED] The header is HONOURED. Unfiltered, this account's token is
offered 111 tools. With the allowlist below, 8.
2. [VERIFIED] It FAILS CLOSED. An allowlist containing one nonsense name
returns 0 tools — an unmatched entry grants nothing rather than voiding
the header and admitting everything. This was the question that mattered
most, because failing open would have meant a typo silently exposed all
111 tools, including remove_dashboard, delete_chart_alert, create_source
and change_team_member_role.
3. [VERIFIED] Matching is NOT exact-name. The seven entries below admitted
eight tools: `monitors` also brought in the singular `monitor`. So an
entry names a CATEGORY, not one tool. It did NOT bring in create_monitor,
so the category is scoped to reads.
4. [VERIFIED] An invalid bearer token is refused with HTTP 401.
The eight tools actually granted are: dashboards, documentation, errors,
incidents, monitor, monitors, query, sources. None of them mutates anything.
Re-run the audit after any Better Stack change — these are observations of a
live service, and a service can change:
node --env-file-if-exists=.env bin/betterstack-mcp-audit.mjs
